quizzes.stem: A team needs an agent to run a task for several hours, survive restarts of its own service, and be resumed the next day, and it does not want to build a sandbox. Which option fits?

options.a: The Client SDK's tool runner, which hosts the sandbox for the loop
options.b: The Messages API alone, which stores the conversation for each request
options.c: The Claude Code CLI, started again by hand each morning
options.d: The hosted harness, which stores sessions on Anthropic's side

explanation.d: The overview table gives "Long-running tasks and asynchronous work" as the best fit, and says sessions "resume cleanly after pauses" with history and outputs stored server-side, so your service holds only an ID.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the Messages API is "Direct model prompting access", for "Custom agent loops and fine-grained control", and you keep the history yourself.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the CLI is something you drive yourself: "You use the CLI by hand."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says the tool runner "drives the same kind of loop inside your process and hosts nothing", while the sandbox belongs to the hosted product.

quizzes.stem: A session is created with an override that lists one tool. The agent itself defines five. How many tools does the session have?

options.a: One, because it takes the place of the whole set
options.b: Five, because an override cannot remove a tool of the agent
options.c: Six, because the override is added to the agent's tools
options.d: Zero, until the agent is updated to a new version

explanation.a: The page says "Overrides never merge with the agent's configuration, so a `tools` override must list every tool the session should have."
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Overrides never merge with the agent's configuration", so nothing is added to the agent's five tools.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "so a tools override must list every tool the session should have", and the agent's own list is not kept.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "They apply to that one session", and nothing waits for a new agent version.

quizzes.stem: A compliance team requires Zero Data Retention for every Claude workload. What follows for Managed Agents?

options.a: It qualifies once the sandbox is self-hosted on the team's network
options.b: It qualifies, because ZDR applies to every endpoint of the API
options.c: It does not qualify, because sessions store history server-side
options.d: It qualifies after the sessions are deleted from the console

explanation.c: The overview says "Managed Agents is not currently eligible for Zero Data Retention or HIPAA Business Associate Agreement (BAA) coverage", because sessions are stateful and stored server-side.
explanation.a: Ruled out because self-hosting moves only the tools: "keep the orchestration on Anthropic's side", so the session data still sits with Anthropic.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the overview says the product is "not currently eligible for Zero Data Retention", not that it is covered.
explanation.d: Ruled out because deleting sessions is a control you hold afterward, and "the data exists on Anthropic's side first", so the product is still not covered.

quizzes.stem: A team creates an environment with `packages` and `limited` networking and lists the registries in `allowed_hosts`, but sets nothing else. What happens?

options.a: The packages install, since the hosts are on the allowed list
options.b: The request is rejected until the registry flag is true
options.c: The environment is created with unrestricted networking instead
options.d: The packages install after a warning that the agent can ignore

explanation.b: The page says "If the environment uses `limited` networking, also set `networking.allow_package_managers` to `true`; otherwise the request is rejected with a 400 error."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page requires "also set `networking.allow_package_managers` to `true`", and listing hosts alone does not open the registries.
explanation.c: Ruled out because only "a create request that omits it gets `unrestricted`", and here the field is set to `limited`.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page names a rejection and not a warning: "otherwise the request is rejected with a 400 error."

quizzes.stem: An agent keeps the default toolset policy and the sandbox has unrestricted networking. What should the team change first?

options.a: Move the agent to a model with a smaller context window
options.b: Switch the toolset to custom tools so that no policy applies
options.c: Add a longer system prompt that forbids any outbound request
options.d: Set bash to `always_ask` and name the allowed hosts

explanation.d: The page advises to "set the `bash` tool's policy to `always_ask` or `auto`", and its first trap says to set `networking` and list the hosts.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Access is granted by host and not by action", so a smaller context window changes neither.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page's advice is to "set the `bash` tool's policy to `always_ask` or `auto`", and a prompt is not a policy.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Custom tools are executed by your application and controlled by you", so they would move the risk into your code and not remove it.

quizzes.stem: A team sets a session budget of `"500"`. The session pauses with a list cost of 503 cents. What does this show?

options.a: A billing error, because the platform must stop exactly at the cap
options.b: Expected behaviour, because the request in flight finishes
options.c: A failed enforcement, because the cap is checked mid-request
options.d: A crash, because a session cannot outlive its budget

explanation.b: The page says "The request in flight when the cap is crossed still finishes", so a paused session can read a fraction past the cap.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "it bounds new work and not the exact total", so the platform is not required to stop at the cap.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A session at its cap does not die", and its history and sandbox are kept.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "The cap is checked between requests, so it bounds new work", which is the designed behaviour and not a failure.

quizzes.stem: A hospital group must keep patient files inside its own network but wants Anthropic to run the agent loop. Which choice fits, and what must the group still do?

options.a: A cloud environment with `unrestricted` networking and a strict system prompt
options.b: A self-hosted sandbox, securing the image and the egress rules itself
options.c: The Messages API with the files pasted into the system prompt of each call
options.d: A cloud environment, since Anthropic hardens it and nothing else is needed

explanation.b: The page says self-hosting moves execution into your infrastructure while "keep the orchestration on Anthropic's side", and that "Without egress restrictions, a compromised tool execution can reach arbitrary external hosts", so the group owns image and egress.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The sandbox can send any request to an allowed host", and `unrestricted` means "Full outbound network access, except for a general safety blocklist", which is the opposite of keeping files inside.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the Messages API is the choice for "Custom agent loops and fine-grained control", and pasting files sends them to Anthropic on every call.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a cloud sandbox runs in Anthropic's infrastructure, where the files would be stored, and the first page lists "self-hosted execution for compliance or data residency" as its own reason to choose another option.

quizzes.stem: A developer migrates an Agent SDK service whose `can_use_tool` callback approved reads and refused pushes. What replaces that callback in Managed Agents?

options.a: A per-tool permission policy, with confirmations sent as events
options.b: The `ClaudeAgentOptions` object, created again for every run
options.c: The environment's `networking` field, which approves each command
options.d: A model override on the session that removes the tool

explanation.a: The first page says `permission_mode` and `can_use_tool` "become a per-tool permission policy", and a paused call is answered with a `user.tool_confirmation` event.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the migration "becomes an agent created once" from that object.
explanation.c: Ruled out because `networking` controls the sandbox's outbound traffic, and "so `networking` does not govern them" for the search and fetch tools.
explanation.d: Ruled out because an override "must list every tool the session should have", and removing a tool is not an approval step.

quizzes.stem: A product relays customers' messages to an agent as `user.message` events and sets the toolset to `auto`. What is the risk?

options.a: Their text counts as the operator's own intent when a call is judged
options.b: The server ignores `user.message` events once a policy is set
options.c: Every call pauses until a person has confirmed it
options.d: A denied call can be overridden by the client with a confirmation

explanation.a: The page says "If you relay untrusted end-user input in `user.message` events, the server reads that input as your intent too."
explanation.b: Ruled out because what you post in `user.message` events "counts as your intent", so the server reads it.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "`auto` is not a human checkpoint", and a safe call "runs before anyone sees it".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a denied call is final: "your client cannot override the denial."

quizzes.stem: A finance team asks for the cost of one long session before approving a budget. Which items does the list cost include?

options.a: Model tokens and the storage of the event history afterward
options.b: Model tokens only, since the sandbox is free to run
options.c: Model tokens, web searches and the running time
options.d: Model tokens and every package the environment installs

explanation.c: The page lists "model tokens at each model's list price, web searches at $10 per 1,000" and "Session running time, at $0.08 per hour".
explanation.b: Ruled out because running time is priced: "Session running time, at $0.08 per hour".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page prices "model tokens at each model's list price", web searches and running time, and no storage.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page names no charge for packages, and prices "what the session consumes" only.
